instruction: Optimize power-entry hot-loop and bulk capacitor placement. `/home/user/Desktop/seed_board.kicad_pcb` is a routable KiCad PCB with fixed anchor parts and movable optimization parts. `/home/user/Desktop/objective.json` describes the optimization objective. Use KiCad command-line tools or KiCad scripting to place/reroute the board as well as possible. Save the optimized board as `/home/user/Desktop/optimized_board.kicad_pcb` and write `/home/user/Desktop/optimization_report.json` summarizing the choices and estimated score. The evaluator returns a continuous score for hot-loop compactness with thermal spacing where higher is better; this is a continuous optimization task; no exact file match is required. Shrink the input hot loop while leaving enough thermal spacing around D1 and L1. The output must remain a valid KiCad 10.0.2 board, preserve every reference and pad/net assignment, keep fixed anchors at their objective coordinates, and pass `kicad-cli pcb drc --severity-all --exit-code-violations`. [Software] Use KiCad CLI tools such as `kicad-cli` and KiCad scripting from the terminal. The installed KiCad tools are `/usr/bin/kicad-cli`, `/usr/bin/pcbnew`, and `/usr/bin/eeschema`; use the one that matches the board or schematic operation.
